review_notes: I reviewed all of lines 1–209 from the supplied text. I did not open other sources, because the file is small and self-contained. The only real candidate is the pair of proofs `Acc.prod_gameAdd` and `Acc.sym2_gameAdd`. Both use a nested induction on two `Acc` hypotheses, with the same outer and inner induction pattern. The second proof works on `Sym2`, so it has four cases from `Sym2.GameAdd`'s disjunction and needs `Sym2.eq_swap` rewrites. `Acc.prod_gameAdd` cannot be reused directly. The `Sym2.GameAdd` relation is not an `InvImage` or `Subrelation` of `Prod.GameAdd` on a quotient. Its predecessor relation is `Prod.GameAdd x y ∨ Prod.GameAdd x.swap y`. A shared lemma would need an abstract two-argument accessibility statement. That lemma would probably be longer than the two proofs it replaced, so I do not count it as a clear improvement. Other repeated shapes are too small to count. These are the `swap`/`eq_swap` rewrites in `GameAdd.fst_snd` and `GameAdd.snd_fst`, the `recursion` and `recursion_eq` pairs, and the `WellFounded.fix` wrappers. They are routine and thin. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
